Q: Error in if, the condition has length > 1 A:

To answer your question directly, it means that if() received a vector with more than one value. Example:

vector= 1:2
if(vector>1.5) {print("big")} else{print("small")

From a logical point of view, it also makes sense. if() is meant to return a single TRUE or a single FALSE which will dictate what pieces of code get executed. But if you give two values it does not know what to do. Is (1,2) bigger or smaller than 1.5?

So to ask if a vector is greater or smaller than a number makes no sense.

But you hint at a similar operation that does make sense, ifelse(). This is an operation that is applying if for every element of vector.

result = ifelse(vector>1.5,"big","small")

is equivalent to:

result= character(2)
for(i in 1:length(vector) {
   if(vector[i]>1.5) {result[i]="big"} else{result[i]="small"}
}

Note that in this for loop we are running as many if() as there are elements in our vector and receiving as many results. So that is a different operation than if(vector>1.5) and a valid one.

Q: Fix the height and width of a column in MJML A:

I put the background-color attribute on the <mj-section>.

It did what I wanted.

Sadly, MJML doesn't support any means of making columns equal height. To get the same effect, maybe you can put the same background-color on the section that you put on the shorter of the columns. It looks consistent that way.

Good luck!

Q: VBA for Excel color codes A:

That's most likely a hex representation of the three color bytes.

  • Numbers prefixed with &H are hexadecimal (aka Base 16).
  • Numbers suffixed with & are unsigned integers.

You'd see it more commonly expressed as an HTML Color Code without the extra characters as #893959, which is the color below. (More about this color here.):

Here's a VBA Function to extract the 3 color bytes and convert from hex to decimal (for use with Excel/VBA) using the RGB Function.

Function Hex2RGB(hex As String) As Long
    Dim r As Long, g As Long, b As Long
    With Application.WorksheetFunction
        r = .Hex2Dec(Mid(hex, 5, 2))
        g = .Hex2Dec(Mid(hex, 7, 2))
        b = .Hex2Dec(Mid(hex, 9, 2))
    End With
    Hex2RGB = RGB(r, g, b)
End Function


Sub Demo()
    Const hexColor = "&H00893959&"
    Debug.Print "The RBG (decimal) interpretation of '" _
        & hexColor & "' is " & Hex2RGB(hexColor) & "."  'returns 5847433
End Sub
